# Post-processing task application plan

## Scope and research

The admitted task T-657e5621-efb8-4c53-8ab9-bdd2a7e6ec69 supplies optional task-editorial and interview applications through the existing ordered plugin engine and shared clarification controller. The selected root and dependency boundary, core-only default, original owner W1/W2/W3 decisions and separate comparison task114 consent remain binding. Current source commit `6725b379`, the task115 source-gap proposal and pinned source acquisition provide the implementation baseline. The plan adds application orchestration inside existing Process/CL operations.

The exact Matt source revision is `4ae2317ddb22b046e26455e4f9c9b3aaaf62212d`. Original `writing-for-agents` entry, `SKILL-MECHANICS.md`, `grill-me` entry, `grilling` sibling and MIT LICENSE form two separately pinned resource closures. Optional adjacent host metadata remains original provenance. The wrapper retains original user-only metadata and literal native Skill requirement. The explicitly selected source-backed adapter translates sibling dispatch and W1 answer routing; native invocation and other-host support retain the actual unqualified state. Task wording uses task-document structure and constraints. Skill/document maintenance remains a separate application.

## Application configuration and atomic publication

Trusted frozen descriptor adaptation and explicit per-occurrence application settings identify task-editorial, task-interview and ordinary compatible contributions. Application roles receive bounded validation; candidate IDs and instruction prose supply no routing authority. Existing package acquisition, parameters, bindings, repeated occurrences, conditions, named boundary mapping and configuration digests remain the generic pipeline. Descriptor suggestions create no installed binding or automatic activation.

Processing preparation outside the writer derives actual selected Pending identities and proposed new/reused T identities from the guarded researched processing proposal. Trusted current requirement preparation freezes matching after-Processing occurrences, package/source/profile/watch identities, conditions, order, parameters and current decision policy. Metadata-only preparation starts no actor. Core-only and excluded/disabled optional configurations retain the current path and require no optional Node/provider capability. The existing transaction rechecks the exact observed identities before publishing.

An enabled applicable post-processing obligation publishes the visible T definition, owned blocking marker, shared CL record and frozen ordered obligations in one recoverable Store.save transaction. Stable task IDs, provenance and task relationships survive all rounds. Exact scope ownership prevents reused or split outputs from stealing another active session. Neither/editor-only/interview-only/both configurations use the same mechanism, with no intermediate implementable Ready interval.

## Contribution, rework and current acceptance

The existing hook prepare/invoke/record/accept sequence owns actual isolated host dispatch and result provenance. The application adapter returns bounded wording proposals, concrete findings or dependent questions. Ordinary guarded CL commands apply task revisions and actual current-mode answers. The same session owns rounds, task revisions, affected rechecks and final specification acceptance. Editor-only semantic questions use core clarification while external interview execution remains absent. Internal questions do not restart the plugin; an explicitly repeated interview occurrence remains a separate configured call.

Application receipts bind the original chain/attempt/result, exact task/session/round and current policy. Required returned questions and findings receive actual guarded answer/revision/resolution evidence. A generic acknowledgement cannot complete the required interview. Multi-round incorporation verifies a contiguous exact revision path from the original stage input to the current task rather than pretending the final TR alone starts at the original input.

Editorial proposals preserve stable identity, Pending/processing provenance, required task sections, constraints and dependencies. Semantic edits reopen affected answers and final acceptance; unrelated settled answers survive. Supported formatting equivalence retains semantic confirmation. An actual later configured editorial occurrence on the current accepted input satisfies the affected wording recheck under the frozen application policy. The explicit A-editor, B-interview, C-editor example executes both editorial occurrences with separate IDs and delivers accepted B additions to C. Matching current C evidence supplies the required recheck without a fabricated duplicate call. Stale wording results and unresolved configured occurrences retain the hold.

Auto consumes actual bounded DG answers and a separate current delegated final specification decision. Manual consumes actual owner answers and confirmation. Current mode, authority and epoch remain guarded; switching reconciles original pending actors and retains history. Fresh factual exploration remains an observed independent prerequisite, including controller-owned delegation translation when nested spawning is unavailable. Unsupported asynchronous/conditional host paths retain visible prerequisites. Out-of-authority choices return to the owner.

Frozen obligations survive cancellation, unavailable or adverse results, transport uncertainty, changed project defaults and package removal. Explicit accepted configuration reconciliation records a distinct policy change; removal/disable supplies no successful answer or invocation. Core/standalone processing handoffs and the existing no-progress stop remain intact.

## Affected editorial recheck execution

The CL record owns an explicit affected editorial recheck mandate. The mandate binds the original registered HC and frozen editorial binding, complete original configuration digest, package/adapter identity, effective JSON parameters and instructions, exact current task input, current mode/authority/epoch and a stable mandate identity. Ordinary project defaults, caller-provided rows or arbitrary completed chains supply no mandate. The core derives the obligation from actual accepted task revisions after the earlier editorial stage. The configured chain runs in the recorded order first; a matching current explicit C/editorial occurrence discharges the obligation once before an additional invocation starts.

If the original A-editor then B-interview chain finishes with affected wording and no matching current C, the core registers one fresh ordinary recheck HC/HI/event under the same CL. The derived chain retains the original full frozen configuration, rows, ordering, package/effective parameters and instructions. The ordinary Node frozen-configuration equality remains binding. A trusted owned CL guard reconstructs the exact origin and authorizes an execution mask for the affected editorial occurrence. The Node dispatcher derives the eligible mask from that actual guarded mandate; a supplied mask or reduced configuration cannot authorize execution. Unmasked stages are explicitly unselected in the derived chain and supply no completion of the original configured occurrences. The original A/B HC/HI, accepted prefix and configured order remain immutable.

Business preparation and completed-readiness obtain the mask through the owned read-only current CL/mandate guard, with the exact observed identities rechecked at the guarded core transition. The generic metadata-only requirement inspection supplies no mask or standalone business authority. An absent, stale, unavailable or ineligible mandated target retains a prerequisite; an empty selection cannot become a successful recheck. Skipped derived stages drain through metadata-only transitions without another actor. Actual changed wording after a recheck can stale the affected mandate/result without replaying B or the original prefix.

The CL readiness verifier binds original and recheck chains to the exact accepted contribution/revision path. A derived recheck that changes wording preserves the original configured chain through an explicit registered selected-task lineage, rather than broadly ignoring older context hashes. The lineage proves contiguous selected-task content/semantic revisions, required settled question revisions/answers, original result and producer evidence, matching current policy and the current affected editorial completion. Unrelated queue changes supply no selected-task revision. The final mechanical-release receipt extends only that verified lineage to the exact released task bytes. Ordinary runtime contexts remain live.

The focused controls include A-B without C, editor-only semantic revision, an actual later repeated editorial occurrence, A-B-C with no fourth invocation, stale/forged/cross-session mandates, changed parameters/source/authority, unselected interview stages in a derived HC, missing mandated capability and unrelated completed-chain substitution. Multi-round B contribution uses actual contiguous CL revision and question/answer evidence; ordinary DG acknowledgement cannot substitute for required answers or rechecks.

## Exact finalization

The visible owned blocking marker/status remains through plugin work and current final acceptance. Finalization removes only the exact recorded controller-owned marker and releases the owned status in the same guarded transaction. A CL-local receipt records before/after content and semantic maps, immutable task/provenance IDs, accepted mode/authority/epoch and exact registered completed HC IDs/hashes. Existing unresolved questions prevent Ready. The proof validates the mechanical transformation byte-for-byte; arbitrary content changes cannot use the mapping.

Original HC input/context/history and original confirmation evidence remain immutable. Readiness and clarification admission may use the explicit finalization mapping only for the exact registered original result and live receipt.after task bytes under current CL acceptance/policy. Ordinary prepare/invoke and new hook contexts always use actual live tasks. Later semantic changes, source/policy drift or unrelated edits retain the established freshness rules and reopen affected obligations. This uses existing CL state and creates no second authoritative ledger or generic status/marker normalization.

## Validation and delivery

The first meaningful failing fixture performs actual temporary owned installation and normal Processing with an enabled matching obligation. The first committed task must already be visibly blocked, linked to the actual CL/frozen requirement and unselectable before an HC starts; current source publishes Ready without CL and fails this behavior. A core-only positive control remains. Original pinned resources form inert fixture prerequisites rather than plugin runtime execution.

Focused tests cover the four configurations; actual ordered A-B-C forwarding; repeated other compatible occurrences and changed order; strict task/provenance/constraint preservation; semantic versus formatting changes; current Auto/Manual answer and acceptance guards; no false interview in editorial-only mode; interrupted, stale, failed, unavailable, cancelled and removed obligations; pending attempts and mode switching; multi-round incorporation; exact mechanical release and adversarial bypasses; standalone installed closure and core-only routing. Synthetic host/owner controls retain the actual classification. Existing actual task118/task127 evidence supplies only the recorded bounded mechanism scope, not new candidate invocation or efficacy.

Task-owned source/check footprints cover every touched helper, runtime, descriptor, reference, resource map and fixture before qualifying checks. Authored templates/common resources drive generation. Required focused checks and source synchronization, strict validation, Python/Node, installer list/dry-run and diff checks precede full independent source review and authorized local commit. Reviewed committed source activates through the owned stopped-handoff installer, preserving canonical state before same-run re-admission. Source/static/synthetic/installed qualification, actual native invocation and comparative recommendations remain separate claims.

## Reviewed implementation footprint

The authored footprint includes `config/plugins/task-editorial.json`, `config/plugins/task-interview.json`, `common/scripts/workflow-state.py`, the existing `common/scripts/plugin-invocation.py` result/incorporation boundary when required, `common/references/future-workflow.md`, `common/references/workflow-metadata.md`, `common/references/plugin-invocation.md`, `templates/operations.json`, the processing tests and pinned fixture resources, applicable installed/copied test controls, and the existing plan/workflow/research documents. A small `common/scripts/plugin-processing.py` helper and matching `config/resource-map.json` entry are permitted if application logic otherwise obscures the existing controller; the helper owns no independent ledger or actor broker. Any necessary Node requirement preparation delta uses the existing runtime/composition/parameter boundaries and matching tests rather than another execution path. Source/fixture closure and concrete task validation footprints receive the same reviewed scope before qualifying checks.
